acceptedFindings.title: No effect size reported despite available data
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: "No estimate-like records were available for p-value/effect-size checks."
stats-run.json: estimates include sum_sq (37.556 for group, 3093.747 residual)
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The ASA statement discourages sole reliance on p-values. An effect size (e.g., eta-squared) is essential to interpret practical importance, especially with a non-significant p-value and a sample of 240.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute and report eta-squared (or partial eta-squared) from the provided sums of squares: eta_sq = 37.556 / (37.556 + 3093.747). Also report a confidence interval if possible.

acceptedFindings.title: No test for homogeneity of variances is reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: ANOVA assumes equal variances across groups; violation can inflate Type I error rates.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report Levene's test or Bartlett's test; if violated, consider Welch's ANOVA or robust methods.

acceptedFindings.title: Homogeneity of variance assumption not checked
evidenceRefs: diagnostics.json: only Shapiro-Wilk, VIF, leverage, Cook's D; no Levene's or Bartlett's test
manuscript.md: no mention of equal variance check
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: ANOVA assumes equal variances across groups. Without verification, the F-test may be invalid, especially if group sizes are unbalanced (unknown). A non-significant Shapiro-Wilk does not address this.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Run Levene's test (or Bartlett's) on the residuals or original outcome by group, and report the result. If violated, consider Welch's ANOVA or transformation.

acceptedFindings.title: Cohort definition insufficiently described
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: only states "240 complete-case records", no eligibility, group sizes, demographics, or source population
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The lack of cohort detail makes it impossible to assess generalizability, potential confounding, or selection biases. It also hinders reproducibility and clinical interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a clear cohort description: inclusion/exclusion criteria, how groups were defined, number per group, any relevant baseline characteristics (age, sex, etc.), and handling of missing data beyond complete-case exclusion.

acceptedFindings.title: Inconsistent statement about estimate availability
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: "No estimate-like records were available for p-value/effect-size checks."
stats-run.json: contains F_statistic, p_value, and sum_sq
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: This contradictory statement misleads readers about the depth of available analysis and undermines trust in the quality control process.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Update the limitations section to accurately reflect that effect size could have been computed but was not, or remove the incorrect sentence.

acceptedFindings.title: No effect size (e.g., eta-squared) reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: A p-value alone does not convey the magnitude of group differences; effect size is essential for interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute and report eta-squared or omega-squared from the ANOVA output.

acceptedFindings.title: Group-level descriptive statistics not provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without means and standard deviations, readers cannot assess direction, magnitude, or data plausibility.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a table of N, mean, SD, and optionally 95% CI for each group.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Could be verified from raw data if available.

acceptedFindings.title: No description of missing data or exclusion criteria
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis can bias results if missingness is not random; the extent and reasons for exclusion need documentation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the number of records excluded, reasons for missingness, and consider sensitivity analysis (e.g., pattern-mixture) or explicitly acknowledge limitation.

acceptedFindings.title: Vague reference to unresolved advisory issues
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: "The methods review found advisory issues that need human review."
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot evaluate whether these issues affect the conclusion. Transparency requires specifying what advisory issues remain.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Either list the specific advisory issues in the limitations or remove the statement if they have been resolved.

acceptedFindings.title: Group variable categories not described
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without naming the groups, the clinical question "Does the continuous outcome differ across clinical groups?" is ambiguous.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Define the group variable and its levels (e.g., control, enhanced treatment, standard treatment) in the manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: No exploration of missing data patterns
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: acknowledges complete-case exclusion may affect result, but no quantification
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: If missingness is non-trivial and related to outcome or group, bias may be introduced. The absence of any missingness analysis weakens the robustness of findings.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the number of excluded records, compare demographics between included and excluded if data allow, or state that missingness was minimal (<5%) and presumed random.

acceptedFindings.title: Figure not referenced or described in manuscript
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Included figures enhance understanding, but if unmentioned, they do not contribute to the narrative.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include the figure in the manuscript with a descriptive caption and in-text reference.

acceptedFindings.title: No prior literature or clinical context discussed
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Lack of contextualization makes the novelty and relevance of the findings unclear.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Briefly mention related studies or the clinical rationale for examining the outcome across these groups.

acceptedFindings.title: No analysis script or raw data provided for independent reproduction
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Reproducibility is a core principle; without code and data, results cannot be independently verified.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a script (e.g., R/Python) that reproduces the analysis from the raw data, or provide a reproducibility package.

acceptedFindings.title: Group sample sizes not reported; possible imbalance unknown
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Unbalanced designs can affect ANOVA’s robustness to assumption violations and power; readers need to know group sizes.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the number of observations per group.
